gaps.sentence: You ___ smoke anywhere inside the building — it is strictly forbidden.
gaps.hint: strictly forbidden, which calls for mustn't

gaps.sentence: The lights are on and I can hear the vacuum cleaner, so someone ___ be at home.
gaps.explanation: Evidence-based certainty uses 'must': must be at home.

gaps.sentence: I ___ see the sea from my bedroom window when I was little.
gaps.explanation: Verbs of perception use 'could' for past ability: could see.

gaps.sentence: He ___ not agree, but let us ask him anyway.
gaps.explanation: 'May' expresses a possibility about the future: may not agree.

gaps.sentence: That ___ be Sarah at the door — she is in Berlin until Friday.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' expresses logical impossibility: can't be Sarah.

gaps.sentence: He ___ not understand the lecture at all yesterday.
gaps.hint: an inability that existed in the past
gaps.explanation: 'Could not' expresses past inability: could not understand.

gaps.sentence: If you want a refund, you ___ keep the receipt — no receipt, no refund.
gaps.hint: a necessity that applies in the future
gaps.explanation: Future necessity uses 'will have to': will have to keep.

gaps.sentence: You ___ better book now — the prices rise every week.
gaps.explanation: 'Had better' gives strong advice, often with urgency: had better book.
